Pre-correction finding on exactly the case you flagged (unavailable observation retaining evidence) - it is NOT safe in the accepted 6969c77f, and the fix is two lines. Sending now so the correction closes it in the same pass.

THE SITES. In cleanupSeatLinkedWorktrees the observation reads are UNGUARDED while every decision around them is guarded:
  const status = sh('git', ['status', '--porcelain=v1', '--ignored', '--untracked-files=all'], row.worktreePath);
  const head   = sh('git', ['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], row.worktreePath);
Compare the neighbours: linkedWorktreeIdentity is wrapped in try/catch -> retained; the snapshot commit is wrapped -> reset then retained; update-ref is wrapped -> retained; worktree remove --force is wrapped -> retained. These two are not.

WHAT HAPPENS, MEASURED. I made a linked worktree's directory unreadable (chmod 000) and ran the same read: it does not return a value, it THROWS - `EACCES spawnSync git EACCES`, because the spawn's own cwd is unreadable. So an unavailable observation propagates a RAW error out of cleanupSeatLinkedWorktrees, which means (a) the pass aborts before rewriteLinkedWorktreeOwnership, so the record keeps the OLD rows and every LATER row in the same record is never examined, and (b) the row is not recorded as retained for the next pass. That is the inverse of the posture the rest of the function keeps, and it is not the typed WorkspacePreservationError a caller expects - it is a raw EACCES out of a reconcile pass.

SMALLEST FIX, the pattern already used four lines above: wrap each read in try/catch and `retained.push(row); continue;`. An unavailable observation then RETAINS with the row kept in the record and a typed retention, and later rows still get their turn. Worth a 568-K test that makes a recorded external worktree unreadable and asserts the typed retention plus the record still carrying the row - that is the evidence flavour you asked me to scrutinize.

#568 correction 91810a5d judged on the platform guards, with the concrete concern for the worker. Full text is swarm context key 'audit/568-correction-platform-guards' (seq 159949); this is the digest.

A - LINUX IS OVER-BROAD, AND MY JUDGMENT IS THAT THIS IS NOT NECESSARY SAFETY. The scan reads every pid in /proc and readlinks /proc/<pid>/cwd; EACCES or EPERM on ANY of them sets observationDenied and then throws 'not observable for every live process', which retains. On any host running anything under another uid - a root process, i.e. every host - a non-root deployment uid gets EACCES and the external worktree is NEVER reclaimed. A guard that can never pass is a restriction nobody can satisfy, the class this swarm removes. Fix, smallest first: scope to process.getuid() so a foreign pid cannot be a holder of our tree; treat ENOENT (a pid that exited mid-scan) as not-a-holder, never as unobservable; keep fail-closed only for a same-uid entry that is genuinely unreadable; and best, ask the coordinator's own live worker pids instead of scanning the host at all - no platform branch, no /proc-hardening dependence.

B - macOS IS THE MIRROR AND THE UNSAFE DIRECTION: the success path never inspects stderr, and lsof exits 0 while warning (unmounted volumes, per-process permission noise), so a PARTIAL enumeration can miss a holder and the tree is then removed under a live process. Fix: scan our uid only (`-u <uid>`), which removes the noise that fills stderr, and treat non-empty stderr as not-authoritative -> retain. Both platforms then read the same: only our processes can block, and an incomplete enumeration of ours fails closed.

C - THE TWO UNGUARDED READS ARE STILL UNGUARDED AT 91810a5d:875 (the git status read, and its rev-parse HEAD sibling). I measured that an unreadable tree throws EACCES out of the cleanup, which aborts the pass before the record rewrite, so later rows are never examined and the row is not carried to the next pass. Two lines: wrap each and retained.push(row); continue;, as linkedWorktreeIdentity
